Thanks Alex — great questions. High-level answers here; Rishi and I can cover details in the technical deep dive.

Isolation model (Dedicated):
- Physical/soft hardware isolation: Dedicated capacity provisions GPU pools reserved to your org. In practice this means we allocate nodes to a tenant pool so there is no co-scheduling of other customers' inference containers on the same GPU hosts. This eliminates most noisy-neighbor cross-tenant interference.
- Network & tenant isolation: optional Private VPC peering available for Dedicated (control plane still managed by Redwood unless you choose the Private package).
- KV cache and model caches are per-tenant in Dedicated so cache eviction from other tenants does not affect you.

SLOs & latency behavior (examples we observe on similar workloads):
- Hosted API (multi-tenant): p50 ~ 40-60ms, p95 ~ 180-250ms, p99 ~ 350-700ms (depends on model & seq-length).
- Dedicated: p50 ~ 30-50ms, p95 ~ 100-180ms, p99 ~ 180-300ms. Tail is significantly improved due to no co-tenancy and reserved capacity.
- Tail protections: we use pre-allocated warm pools, cross-request batching limits, and enforced per-tenant concurrency to prevent a single tenant from monopolizing scheduler throughput.

Autoscaling & scale-up:
- Dedicated pools support autoscaling with warm buffer sizing. Typical scale-up time for adding warm nodes is ~45-90s depending on model size; for bursty spiky traffic we recommend a small always-on buffer (configurable).

Private / VPC option:
- Private (VPC) option gives you network-level isolation and the option to route egress through your network appliances. Control plane remains Redwood-managed unless you contract the on-prem bundle.
